statement: A point is at coordinates (2, 3). It is moved 4 right and 5 down. Where does it end up?

choices.misconception: I added the downward move instead of subtracting it.
I applied the move down but left out the move to the right.
I applied the horizontal move but left the vertical one out.
I subtracted the rightward move and added the downward one, reversing both.

hints: Right adds to the first number and down subtracts from the second.
Handle the two directions separately. Moving right increases the first coordinate and moving down decreases the second, so apply one move at a time and keep the signs straight.
2 + 4 gives the first coordinate, and 3 - 5 gives the second.

solutions.reliable: Moving 4 right takes the first coordinate from 2 to 6, and moving 5 down takes the second from 3 to minus 2, giving (6, minus 2). The transferable idea: treat the two coordinates independently and let the direction fix the sign, rather than trying to picture the whole move at once.

whyOnTest: Sign errors on the vertical move are the whole difficulty here, and each one-move-only answer is offered.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
